subject: history
intro: History leads to paid work interrogating the past for a living — researching and writing it, keeping its records and objects safe for the public, editing the books it appears in, and teaching it.

roles.title: Historians
roles.what: Research, analyse, record and interpret the past as recorded in sources — government and institutional records, newspapers and periodicals, photographs, interviews and films — and present the findings to others.
roles.where: The sourcework at the heart of this syllabus — questioning why events happened, weighing causes and judging what changed, from 1848's revolutions to the road to the First World War — is the method historians apply professionally.

roles.title: Archivists
roles.what: Appraise, edit and direct the safekeeping of permanent records and historically valuable documents, and take part in research activities based on the archival materials they hold.
roles.where: The syllabus's constant work with primary evidence — war records, treaties, speeches and newspapers behind the unification and civil-war units — trains the instinct for what documents matter and how to preserve and order them.

roles.title: History Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach human history and historiography courses at colleges and universities — lecturing on the periods and themes they research, leading seminars and marking, and publishing scholarship of their own.
roles.where: The course's nineteenth-century arc — revolutions, Italian and German unification, the American Civil War, empire and the First World War — is exactly the survey material these teachers cover in modern-history modules.

roles.title: Editors
roles.what: Plan, coordinate and revise written material for publication — reviewing proposals and drafts, shaping structure and argument, and checking the accuracy of what will appear in print or online.
roles.where: Essay writing built on evidence — the syllabus's sustained written arguments about causes, consequences and significance — trains the structural judgement editors apply to other people's manuscripts.
